doc.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Planned 1998 JVC tribute to Jimmy, and forgotten trad players
summary: Jimmy was born in 1907; she laments that artists like Bobby Hackett and Wild Bill Davison are no longer heard and describes the June 1998 JVC festival tribute she is hosting.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: You say he replaced Bix Beiderbecke at age 17. Refresh our memories of what year Jimmy was born.
So he and Benny Carter are the same year.

Yeah, God!, Benny Carter. Then he started . . . There’s a lot of records that he made with Tommy Dorsey, and a whole bunch of things. George Avakian was recording a lot in those days. He’s still around and still doing it, but he was a pretty young cat at that time. I’m glad we’re doing this thing at the festival, in tribute to Jimmy, because some of the people of that era, when they die, they just drop out of sight. I’ve never heard of Bobby . . . I’ve never heard anything by Bobby Hackett again since he died.

Yeah, and Wild Bill. I think the only reason you ever hear something by Wild Bill is his wife is always pushing and promoting something, but you hardly ever hear anything, and you don’t ever hear anything by Jimmy either.

By the way, for our listeners, Marian is referring to the 1998 JVC Jazz Festival, which is on June 22nd, will be a tribute to Mr. Jimmy McPartland, hosted by Marian and a myriad of guests and associates who were either close associates of Jimmy’s, but, or influenced by his style.

All the people that worked with him, I think I’ve managed to collect. All of them. All the people who did work with him from time to time, like Eddie Locke on drums. Bill Crow worked with him a lot. Howard Alden. Warren Vaché. Jimmy admired Warren Vaché a great deal.
